script.text: A personalized cancer vaccine just beat the standard drug alone. By how much?

Moderna and Merck report a phase three melanoma trial. Surgeons had removed the tumors of eleven hundred thirty seven patients. Two thirds then got the vaccine plus Keytruda. One third got Keytruda and a placebo. Each vaccine is made from the patient's own tumor mutations.

The companies say it cut the risk of the cancer returning, or death, by forty two percent. For spread to distant organs, or death, the figure was thirty eight percent. After two years, eighty two percent of the combination group had no recurrence. Against seventy percent.
These are company figures, shown at a cancer meeting in Madrid. A peer reviewed paper is not yet confirmed. Some analysts hoped for more. The vaccine is experimental and not approved.
Will personalized cancer vaccines win approval within five years? Yes or no?

upload.title: Moderna-Merck Cancer Vaccine Beats Keytruda Alone #shorts
upload.description:
Moderna and Merck report that their personalized mRNA melanoma vaccine, given with Keytruda, cut the risk of recurrence or death by 42% versus Keytruda alone in a phase 3 trial of 1,137 patients. These are company-reported figures presented at the ESMO meeting; the therapy is investigational and not approved.

Sources: Merck / Moderna announcements (INTerpath-001); BioSpace; Endpoints News; CNBC; AJMC.
